subject: Request: SLA exception for canary rollout — VectorCloud deployment
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@vectorcloud.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: VectorCloud Legal <legal@vectorcloud.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Canary deployment and SLA questions

Hi Sean,

We are close to the beta deployment window next week and I wanted to align on a couple of things before we flip traffic. Our security and SRE teams pushed back on the plan because the canary will run a new quantized runtime (q4_0) and a slightly different kernel path than our production model. That means there is a small, but measurable, risk of latency regressions for the first 48–72 hours.

Two asks from VectorCloud:
- Can Redwood provide an SLA exception window during the canary so that standard latency SLO penalties do not apply?
- We need an automatic fallback/pinning promise: if p95 latency exceeds 350 ms for two consecutive 15-minute windows, traffic must automatically be shifted back to the prior stable variant.

I attached the canary rollout doc and the dashboard snapshot the SREs referenced. Let me know if you can confirm these controls and whether Redwood needs a signed amendment.

Thanks,
Raj
Sr. PM, VectorCloud

Attachments: canary-plan-v2.pdf (application/pdf), latency-dashboard.png (image/png)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@vectorcloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Canary deployment and SLA questions

Raj — thanks for the heads-up and the docs. We're aligned on the importance of a safe canary. Quick summary of what Redwood can commit to operationally: 

1) Exception window: We can agree to a 72-hour SLA carve-out during the canary start (traffic ramp). During that window we will not automatically apply financial penalties for transient latency bumps provided the rollout follows the agreed plan.
2) Auto-fallback: We will enable an automated traffic switch that re-pins to the prior stable model if p95 > 350 ms for two consecutive 15-min windows. That action will be logged and trigger an incident notification to both teams.
3) Guardrails: We'll run the canary behind an A/B split with a progressive ramp (2%, 10%, 50%, 100%) and a hard stop at any step if error rate or p95 breaches thresholds.

To proceed I need an internal SLA exception approved (legal + ops) and a signed addendum covering the fallback action. Laura — can you review and confirm language for a 72-hour carve-out and the automatic rollback clause? Aditya — can infra prepare the failure-detection rule and automated rollback runbook?

Raj — if that sounds ok, we can draft the addendum and share it for legal review today.

—Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On attachments: I reviewed the plan; minor request — add explicit telemetry hooks (token-level latency, kernel-path tag) so rollback can be unambiguous.

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Canary deployment and SLA questions

Thanks Sean. I spoke with Legal — we can do a temporary SLA carve-out but need:
- A precisely worded addendum limited to the deployment window (start/end times + conditions).
- A clause that the customer cannot claim prior incidents during the carve-out as grounds for termination.
- Confirmation that the automatic fallback is reversible only by the Redwood on-call or an authorized VectorCloud SRE after post-mortem sign-off.

I'll draft the addendum. One point to raise with product: we should add a pin-by-model-hash capability in the rollout API to ensure we can re-pin to an exact binary. Marissa — can you confirm whether the console supports model-hash pinning today or if this requires a short runtime patch?

Laura
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

> On Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 10:03 AM Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Raj — thanks for the heads-up and the docs. We're aligned on the importance of a safe canary...

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Canary deployment and SLA questions

Laura — quick update from Product/Runtime: we already support pin-by-hash in Dedicated and Hosted—there's an API field model_hash. Two notes: 
- The automated rollback flow will reuse the previous model_hash stored in the release metadata; we'll confirm metadata retention for 14 days.
- The new quantized runtime path is behind a runtime flag; infra will toggle it for the canary. Aditya, please confirm the flagging and the metric emission (kernel_tag) so the thresholding rule can reference it.

I also attached a small runbook snippet (see canary-plan-v2.pdf) describing the A/B split percentages and the emergency rollback procedure. If VectorCloud wants a write-access view in Console we can provide a viewer link for their SREs.

Marissa
PM, Runtime

> On Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 08:22 AM laura_bennett@redwood.com wrote:
> > Thanks Sean. I spoke with Legal — we can do a temporary SLA carve-out but need...

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 13:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Canary deployment and SLA questions

All — infra confirms:
- The kernel_tag and model_hash are emitted to tracing; we'll create a detection rule that checks p95(latency) grouped by kernel_tag.
- Auto-fallback will be implemented as an automated traffic policy that executes a re-pin to the stored model_hash and sets the canary flag to "paused." It will create a change event and post to the incident Slack channel #ops-vectorcloud.
- We'll also expose a single-click rollback in the Console for VectorCloud SREs (viewer + on-call confirmation).

I've attached the draft detection rule and the query we'll use in the runbook (see canary-plan-v2.pdf). Ops will schedule a tabletop tomorrow to validate.

Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer

> On Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 11:40 AM marissa_cole@redwood.com wrote:
> > Laura — quick update from Product/Runtime: we already support pin-by-hash...

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@vectorcloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Canary deployment and SLA questions

Raj — thanks for the patience. Summary and next steps: 

- Redwood will provide a 72-hour SLA carve-out during the canary ramp that prevents financial penalties for transient latency regressions so long as the canary follows the documented plan.
- Auto-fallback will be enforced automatically (re-pin to prior model_hash) if p95 > 350 ms for two consecutive 15-minute windows; this triggers incident notification and requires a post-mortem before permanent changes.
- Legal will issue a one-page addendum for signature. I'll loop VectorCloud Legal once Laura posts the draft.
- Ops and Product will run a tabletop Friday at 11:00 PT; invite to follow.

If VectorCloud signs the addendum we'll treat this as an approved exception and proceed with the canary on Monday.

Best,
Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On attachments: canary-plan-v2.pdf, latency-dashboard.png
